summary:
I finished crates/search-analysis and fixed the bugs that new Elasticsearch-derived tests turned up. Clippy with -D warnings is clean and cargo test passes: 71 unit tests, all 19,050 fixture cases (2 known divergences), and the allocation test.

The previous session left the crate not compiling partway through a switch of simple_pattern to a new Lucene RegExp engine; I finished that switch and recorded its fixtures (lucene_regexp.json).

I added 23 fixture groups: every component name in every role, every parameter with ill-typed values, unused definitions, *_path settings, request parsing, a Unicode sweep, long texts, plus random chains, index settings, synonyms and HTML. They found these bugs, all now fixed:
- **Final offsets:** several tokenizers reported the wrong final offset when a `limit` filter stopped reading early.
- **Unicode:** Java regex classes used Unicode 16 instead of 17; the thai tokenizer missed a JDK quirk in its character categories; normalizers deleted supplementary format characters.
- **UTF-16 counting:** stemmers counted code points or bytes where Lucene counts UTF-16 units.
- **Snowball:** English and Italian lacked changes from the Snowball version Lucene 10.5.1 ships. All stemmers and analyzers now match Elasticsearch on the full Snowball test vocabularies (about 2M words).
- **Settings:** empty booleans, default stop words with ignore_case, min_hash with_rotation, pattern_capture patterns, and synonyms precedence.
- **Component names:** keyword_repeat/type_as_payload as an inline `type`, hunspell errors, the `chinese` analyzer type, the edgeNGram message.
- **Validation:** errors are now reported in Elasticsearch's order; errors Lucene raises only when a stream is created now appear only when an analyzer uses the component. The full error chain and root_cause now match.
- **Other:** *_path settings now get Elasticsearch's file-access errors; `_analyze` request type checks; token limit error type; negative position_increment_gap; char_group's explain attributes; fingerprint with empty terms; truncate through a surrogate pair.

New public APIs: analyzer wrappers for index_prefixes, index_phrases and search_as_you_type subfields (search_as_you_type checked against Elasticsearch), `warm_up()`, `is_java_exception()`.

Release throughput per core (about 8 MB in 4 KB documents): standard analyzer about 150 MB/s (17M tokens/s), whitespace about 270 MB/s, english about 90 MB/s. Snowball analyzers are slower: russian 40–50 MB/s, dutch about 28 MB/s. Lucene's standard analyzer runs at tens of MB/s per core. Large synonym sets are fast: 100k rules build in 0.35 s.
public_api:
crate search_analysis (used by search-es; search-index depends on it):
- Analysis::from_settings(&serde_json::Value /* index.analysis, nested or dotted */, &IndexOptions) -> Result<Analysis, AnalysisError>. It validates in Elasticsearch's build order (char filters, tokenizers, filters, analyzer types, normalizer types, then custom analyzers and custom normalizers, each in Java HashMap order). Errors Lucene raises only when a stream is created are reported only when an analyzer uses the component.
- Analysis::global() -> &'static Analysis; Analysis::global_with(IndexOptions) -> Analysis.
- Analysis lookups: analyzer(name), search_analyzer(name), default_analyzer(), default_search_analyzer(), default_search_quote_analyzer(), normalizer(name), whitespace_normalizer(name), build_ad_hoc_json(&{tokenizer, filter, char_filter}).
- Analysis::analyze(&AnalyzeRequest, field_analyzer: Option<&Analyzer>, AnalyzeLimits{max_token_count, max_char_count}) -> Result<serde_json::Value> returns the full `_analyze` body, including explain `detail`.
- AnalyzeRequest::from_json(&Value): ObjectParser type rules and texts, without the [line:col] prefix (the REST layer adds it). NameOrDefinition.
- Analyzer (Arc inside, Send + Sync, pooled chains, no per-token allocation):
  - analyze(text, &mut dyn FnMut(&Token)); analyze_values(&[&str], sink); try_analyze; try_analyze_values; terms; normalize
  - explain(texts, attributes) -> Explain; explain_limited(texts, attributes, max_tokens)
  - position_increment_gap() -> i32 (CHANGED from u32; may be negative, as in ES); offset_gap() -> u32
  - analysis_mode(); check_allowed_in_mode(mode); name(); is_custom()
  - NEW field-mapper wrappers: with_index_prefixes(min_chars, max_chars, position_increment_gap: i32) -> Analyzer (text `._index_prefix`); with_index_phrases(position_increment_gap: i32) -> Analyzer (text `._index_phrase`, 2-token shingles, `_` filler); with_shingles(n: 2..=4) -> Result<Analyzer> (search_as_you_type `._Ngram`); with_shingles_and_prefixes(max_shingle_size) -> Result<Analyzer> (search_as_you_type `._index_prefix`). Wrapper gaps follow ES: index_prefixes/phrases take the field's gap; search_as_you_type uses the inner analyzer's own gap (a custom analyzer's position_increment_gap, 0 for built-ins).
- Token<'a> { term, start_offset, end_offset (UTF-16), position, position_increment, position_length, kind, keyword, payload }.
- Explain / TokenList / ExplainToken / CharFilteredText with to_json(); Normalizer::normalize, Normalizer::analyzer.
- IndexOptions { version, max_ngram_diff, max_shingle_diff, scripts: Option<Arc<dyn ScriptHost>>, synonym_sets: Option<Arc<dyn SynonymSets>>, max_token_count, index_name }.
- Hooks: trait ScriptHost::compile_predicate(&Value) -> Arc<dyn TokenPredicate>; trait TokenPredicate::test(&ScriptToken); trait SynonymSets::rules(set) -> Option<Vec<String>> (Solr format).
- AnalysisError { kind, reason, status, caused_by }: to_json() (an empty reason renders as null, i.e. Java's null message); root_cause() follows ES guessRootCauses (descends only through ES-exception causes). NEW pub fn is_java_exception(kind) -> bool.
- ThaiDictionary::{from_words, from_jdk}; set_thai_dictionary(d).
- NEW pub fn warm_up(): builds the lazily compiled global scanners; uax_url_email alone takes about 0.4 s.
done: Finished the switch to the Lucene RegExp engine (src/lregexp.rs) that the previous session left not compiling: simple_pattern/simple_pattern_split run on RunAutomaton with an ASCII transition table. Fixed SimplePatternTokenizer's end-of-input rule to match Lucene. Replaced the ad-hoc zz_tmp.json with a generated lucene_regexp group (832 cases).
Fixed the fingerprint filter allocating per token (arena plus sorted ranges, so the steady-state allocation test passes again). Fixed fingerprint so an empty term adds no separator.

Final offsets: with `limit` stopping early, char tokenizers report the last token's end; standard, classic and uax report the scanner position; simple_pattern reports how far it read; thai reports the end of the current chunk. Covered by the stream_end group (304 cases).

Component names: an inline {type: X} falls back to the pre-configured component (keyword_repeat, type_as_payload). Hunspell now gives Elasticsearch's errors. `chinese` is accepted as an analyzer type. The edgeNGram pre-configured tokenizer has the right message. Covered by the registry and registry_index groups (2,640 cases).

Settings parsing: empty or blank booleans fall back to the default. Default stop words are used as-is (ignore_case only applies to configured words). min_hash with_rotation uses Java's Boolean.parseBoolean. delimited_payload float errors match. An empty pattern_replace char filter pattern counts as missing. pattern_capture `patterns` is not comma-split. The synonyms empty-string NPE and an empty type_table list (NoSuchElementException with a null reason) are reproduced. Covered by params (3,036 cases) and params_index (552).
Negative position_increment_gap is supported; Analyzer::position_increment_gap() now returns i32.

Errors whose components Elasticsearch only creates on use (tokenizer max_token_length, keyword buffer_size, ngram gram sizes, pattern group, path_hierarchy skip/buffer, every simple_pattern error, lowercase language, length, limit, decompounder sizes, synonym rule loading) are now lazy. They surface when an analyzer uses the component, via the new LazyError factory.

from_settings follows Elasticsearch's validation order, including Java HashMap iteration order. Checked by params_unused (1,769 cases), index_fuzz (300) and 1,200 extra seeded cases that were not committed.
Error chains: the fixture test now compares the full caused_by chain and root_cause. Added the snowball class_not_found causes and the request parse causes, and implemented ES root-cause semantics.

*_path settings follow Elasticsearch's path handling: Java Path.resolve, entitlement-denied paths (server vs analysis-common readable directories), directories ('Is a directory'), missing files, and the synonyms_path variants. Covered by paths (108 cases).

`_analyze` request parsing (from_json) follows ObjectParser's field type rules. The token-limit error type is now status_exception, and the harness applies index analyze limits. Covered by request (55 cases).

Unicode 17: Java regex properties come from our JDK tables instead of regex-syntax's Unicode 16. The thai tokenizer reproduces the JDK break-iterator category quirk (unassigned gaps before CJK extensions count as letters). Covered by the unicode group (1,200 cases).

UTF-16 fidelity: every char[]-port and Snowball stemmer gets supplementary characters as stand-in surrogate pairs, so length, cursor and region tests count UTF-16 units. German and Brazilian isStemmable reject surrogates. Dutch and Serbian literal cursor positions count units, not bytes. truncate through a surrogate pair yields U+FFFD. Normalizers no longer delete supplementary format characters. Covered by unicode2 (714 cases).

Snowball: ported the changes Lucene 10.5.1's snapshot has (English aeo undoubling rule, Italian divano exception). All 29 Snowball languages, every stemmer language and every language analyzer match Elasticsearch on the full snowball-data vocabularies (about 2M words; checked once, not committed). A 1,500-word sample per language is committed as stem_vocab.
Fixed char_group explain: it has no termFrequency attribute, as Elasticsearch builds it with the plain attribute factory.

New FixedShingleFilter and GraphTokenFilter port (Lucene 10.5.1 semantics) in src/filter/fixed_shingle.rs, plus TrailingShingle. Used by the new Analyzer wrappers. search_as_you_type subfields match Elasticsearch (225 cases including synonyms and stop-word gaps).
Added warm_up(). Sped up eager DFA construction (one pass per DFA state, foldhash).

Fixture infrastructure: cases one per line (17 MB in total), shared texts ({"$text": key}), compact FNV digests for long or large outputs, FIXTURES_DUMP, location-insensitive parse error comparison, dictionary-dependent skipping for limited thai cases.

Regression and fuzz groups: chains_fuzz (700 committed; 9,000 more seeded cases run, which found the fingerprint bug and otherwise only the known min_hash lone-surrogate divergence), synonyms_fuzz (400), html_fuzz (300), long (268), regressions (4).

Updated docs/search/contracts.md (search-analysis section): i32 gap, the wrappers, warm_up, is_java_exception, null reason, Snowball notes. Ran cargo fmt on the crate. Left no analysis-* indices or templates on the reference cluster.
remaining: Thai segmentation without the JDK dictionary: the built-in word list is ICU's, because the JDK's thai_dict is GPL. Installing it with set_thai_dictionary (or ROLL_THAI_JDK_DICT in tests) gives exact output; every thai case matches with it.

Lone surrogates: Rust strings cannot hold the lone surrogate that min_hash (or a cut surrogate pair) leaves in a term, so we hold U+FFFD. A later word_delimiter then splits differently from Java. Known divergence: chains_fuzz/chain/598.
jregex \N{name}: Java's Unicode character-name table is not included, so such patterns are rejected. Known divergence: regex_props/other/named.

Normalizer create-time errors are checked per normalizer as it is built. Elasticsearch checks them after all normalizers are built, so with several invalid normalizers a different error can be reported first.

uax_url_email compiles its URL grammar (about 8,500 DFA states) in about 0.4 s on first use per process. warm_up() moves this off the request path; precomputing the tables at build time would remove it.
Snowball stemmers cost about 150–300 ns per word (dutch analyzer about 28 MB/s, russian 40–50 MB/s). The runtime could be optimized (ASCII fast paths in among search and grouping).

Completion suggester analysis (Lucene's ConcatenateGraphFilter / CompletionAnalyzer) is not provided. `_analyze` cannot reach completion fields, so the suggester implementer must verify it through suggest results.

Hunspell, hyphenation_decompounder dictionaries and the analysis plugins (icu, kuromoji, nori, smartcn, phonetic) are not implemented. Hunspell and hyphenation_decompounder reject their configuration as a node without the files does.
tests: `cargo clippy -p search-analysis --all-targets -- -D warnings` gives 0 warnings. `cargo test -p search-analysis` passes. Unit tests: 71 pass. Fixtures: 1 test over 19,050 Elasticsearch 9.5.5 `_analyze` cases in 38 groups, all matching plus 2 known divergences (\N{name}, the min_hash lone surrogate). It compares tokens, offsets, positions, explain attributes, error type, reason and status, the full caused_by chain and root_cause. With ROLL_THAI_JDK_DICT, the thai cases (including long, limited and chunked texts) also all match. perf: steady_state_allocates_nothing passes (49 analyzers and chains, 0 allocations after warm-up); throughput and synonym_build_time are ignored by default. Last release run: tokenizers alone at standard 205, whitespace 262, classic 311, uax_url_email 193, letter 268 MB/s. Analyzers: standard 154 MB/s (17M tokens/s), whitespace 273, english 91, russian 44, dutch 28, thai 53, synonym-graph chain 45, char-filter/stemmer chain 36 MB/s. 100k synonym rules build in 0.35 s. Checked once, not committed: the full snowball-data vocabularies (about 2M words) through every Snowball language, stemmer language and language analyzer match Elasticsearch, and 9,000 extra random chains plus 1,200 extra random index settings match apart from the known min_hash divergence.
notes_for_others: search-server / search-es: call search_analysis::warm_up() at process start on a background thread. Otherwise the first request that uses uax_url_email pays about 0.4 s to compile its grammar.

search-es: Analyzer::position_increment_gap() now returns i32 (it can be negative, as in Elasticsearch). An AnalysisError with an empty reason stands for Java's null message (to_json renders "reason": null); es_error should do the same. search_analysis::is_java_exception(kind) is the list of plain Java exception types, so JAVA_EXCEPTIONS in search-es/src/analysis.rs can use it. AnalysisError::root_cause() implements guessRootCauses.
search-es: the `_analyze` token-limit error type is now status_exception, as Elasticsearch returns. Pass index.analyze.max_token_count and max_char_count in AnalyzeLimits.

search-index / search-es mappers: build subfield analyzers with the new wrappers. text index_prefixes: analyzer.with_index_prefixes(min_chars, max_chars, field_position_increment_gap). text index_phrases: analyzer.with_index_phrases(field_gap). search_as_you_type `._Ngram`: index or search analyzer .with_shingles(n). search_as_you_type `._index_prefix`: index analyzer .with_shingles_and_prefixes(max_shingle_size); its search analyzer is search_analyzer.with_shingles(max_shingle_size), as in Elasticsearch.

Index creation: Analysis::from_settings now reports the error Elasticsearch reports first when several definitions are invalid. Definitions whose errors Lucene raises only on use are accepted while no analyzer uses them, as in Elasticsearch.

Fixtures: regenerate with `python3 -I crates/search-analysis/tests/fixtures/gen_fixtures.py http://127.0.0.1:19200 crates/search-analysis/tests/fixtures [group…]`. snowball_vocab and stem_vocab need SNOWBALL_VOCAB_DIR. FIXTURES=<substr>, FIXTURES_VERBOSE=1 and FIXTURES_DUMP=<file> help with diagnosis.
Licensing: the JDK thai_dict is GPL and must not be committed. Install it at runtime via set_thai_dictionary if exact Thai segmentation is wanted.
